simple.meaning: פָּרָשׁ (pârâsh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a steed (as stretched out to a vehicle, not single nor for mounting ); also (by implication) a driver (in a chariot), i.e. (collectively) cavalry.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 57 times across Genesis, Exodus, Joshua, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, and 14 more, beginning at Genesis 50:9. Its contexts include Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּרָשׁ (H6571).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: פָּרָשׁ (pârâsh) / H6571 is traced through Genesis 50:9, Exodus 14:9, Exodus 14:17, Exodus 14:18 as a generated source-based concept entry.
